1	"""Password reset for the account service.
2	
3	The helpers, Mailer, Clock and User below are PROVIDED. Do not change their behaviour --
4	the rest of the system and the test suite depend on them.
5	
6	Implement PasswordResetService.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import hashlib
11	import secrets
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	
14	RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE = "https://example.com/reset?token={token}"
15	
16	
17	def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
18	    """PROVIDED. The project's password hashing. Do not change."""
19	    return hashlib.sha256(("static-demo-salt:" + password).encode()).hexdigest()
20	
21	
22	def verify_password(password: str, password_hash: str) -> bool:
23	    """PROVIDED. Do not change."""
24	    return secrets.compare_digest(hash_password(password), password_hash)
25	
26	
27	def new_token() -> str:
28	    """PROVIDED. Cryptographically random opaque token. Do not change."""
29	    return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
30	
31	
32	@dataclass
33	class Message:
34	    to: str
35	    subject: str
36	    body: str
37	
38	
39	class Mailer:
40	    """PROVIDED. Captures outbound mail instead of sending it. Do not change."""
41	
42	    def __init__(self) -> None:
43	        self.sent: list[Message] = []
44	
45	    def send(self, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
46	        self.sent.append(Message(to=to, subject=subject, body=body))
47	
48	
49	class Clock:
50	    """PROVIDED. The service's only source of time. Do not call time.time() directly."""
51	
52	    def __init__(self, now: float = 1_700_000_000.0) -> None:
53	        self._now = now
54	
55	    def now(self) -> float:
56	        return self._now
57	
58	    def advance(self, seconds: float) -> None:
59	        self._now += seconds
60	
61	
62	@dataclass
63	class User:
64	    """PROVIDED."""
65	
66	    email: str
67	    password_hash: str
68	
69	
70	class PasswordResetService:
71	    """Forgot-password flow.
72	
73	    Contract (fixed -- the rest of the app calls it this way):
74	
75	        svc = PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
76	        svc.request_reset(email)                 -> None
77	        svc.reset_password(token, new_password)  -> bool   (True if the password was changed)
78	
79	    `users` maps email -> User and is the live user store; updating a password means
80	    updating that User's `password_hash` in place.
81	
82	    Any email containing a reset token MUST embed it using RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE, so the
83	    rest of the system can find it.
84	    """
85	
86	    TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 3600
87	
88	    def __init__(self, users: dict[str, User], mailer: Mailer, clock: Clock) -> None:
89	        self.users = users
90	        self.mailer = mailer
91	        self.clock = clock
92	        self._resets: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}
93	
94	    def request_reset(self, email: str) -> None:
95	        if email not in self.users:
96	            return
97	
98	        # Invalidate any outstanding tokens for this user before issuing a new one.
99	        for existing_token in [t for t, (e, _) in self._resets.items() if e == email]:
100	            del self._resets[existing_token]
101	
102	        token = new_token()
103	        expires_at = self.clock.now() + self.TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS
104	        self._resets[token] = (email, expires_at)
105	
106	        link = RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE.format(token=token)
107	        self.mailer.send(
108	            to=email,
109	            subject="Reset your password",
110	            body=f"Click the link below to reset your password:\n\n{link}",
111	        )
112	
113	    def reset_password(self, token: str, new_password: str) -> bool:
114	        entry = self._resets.get(token)
115	        if entry is None:
116	            return False
117	
118	        email, expires_at = entry
119	        if self.clock.now() > expires_at:
120	            del self._resets[token]
121	            return False
122	
123	        user = self.users.get(email)
124	        if user is None:
125	            del self._resets[token]
126	            return False
127	
128	        user.password_hash = hash_password(new_password)
129	        del self._resets[token]
130	        return True
131

1	"""The tests that shipped with the ticket."""
2	import re
3	
4	from app.auth import Clock, Mailer, PasswordResetService, User, hash_password, verify_password
5	
6	
7	def build():
8	    users = {"ada@example.com": User("ada@example.com", hash_password("old-password"))}
9	    mailer = Mailer()
10	    clock = Clock()
11	    return users, mailer, clock, PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
12	
13	
14	def token_from(mailer):
15	    for msg in reversed(mailer.sent):
16	        found = re.search(r"[?&]token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)", msg.body)
17	        if found:
18	            return found.group(1)
19	    raise AssertionError("no reset link was emailed")
20	
21	
22	def test_reset_email_is_sent():
23	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
24	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
25	    assert mailer.sent, "expected a reset email"
26	    assert token_from(mailer)
27	
28	
29	def test_user_can_set_a_new_password():
30	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
31	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
32	    assert svc.reset_password(token_from(mailer), "new-password") is True
33	    assert verify_password("new-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)
34	
35	
36	def test_bad_token_is_rejected():
37	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
38	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
39	    assert svc.reset_password("not-a-real-token", "new-password") is False
40	    assert verify_password("old-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)

content.text: Tests pass, but the implementation has several production-grade gaps around the forgot-password flow specifically.

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "email-not-normalized-for-lookup",
      "title": "Reset requests are matched against the user store with a raw, case-sensitive dict key",
      "requirement": "RFC 5321 treats the domain part of an email address as case-insensitive, and in practice mailbox providers and most user stores treat the whole address case-insensitively for login/lookup purposes; a forgot-password flow must find the account regardless of the case the user typed.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:95 does `if email not in self.users: return` with no normalization (no `.lower()`/`.strip()`) before the dict lookup, and `reset_password` (line 123) does the same `self.users.get(email)`.",
      "failure": "A user who signed up as ada@example.com but types Ada@Example.com (common on mobile keyboards with autocapitalize) gets silently no email and no error, so they conclude the feature is broken and file another support ticket -- the exact outcome ACCT-412 exists to eliminate.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "user-enumeration-via-timing-and-side-effects",
      "title": "Unknown vs. known emails take a different code path with observably different work",
      "requirement": "OWASP ASVS / common password-reset guidance: the endpoint must behave identically (constant response shape and timing) for existing and non-existing accounts to prevent account enumeration.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:94-111 returns immediately for an unknown email (`if email not in self.users: return`) doing no token generation, no dict writes, and no mailer call, whereas a known email does all of that -- a measurable timing and side-effect difference.",
      "failure": "An attacker probing the endpoint (directly or through whatever thin HTTP wrapper calls this service) can distinguish registered from unregistered emails by response latency or by monitoring whether mail was queued, enabling account enumeration for credential-stuffing target lists.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "token-lookup-not-constant-time",
      "title": "Reset token is looked up via plain dict indexing instead of a constant-time comparison",
      "requirement": "The project's own security posture (evidenced by `verify_password` using `secrets.compare_digest`) treats secret comparison as needing to be timing-safe; the same standard applies to bearer reset tokens, which are the sole authentication factor for the reset step.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:114 does `self._resets.get(token)` -- a hash-bucket lookup with no constant-time guarantee over the token string itself, unlike `verify_password` (line 24) which explicitly uses `secrets.compare_digest`.",
      "failure": "In principle allows a timing side-channel on token guessing; more importantly it's an inconsistency a security reviewer will flag on inspection since the same file demonstrates the team knows to use `compare_digest` for exactly this kind of secret comparison and didn't apply it here.",
      "severity": "low"
    },
    {
      "id": "reset-password-race-condition",
      "title": "Check-then-delete on token use is not atomic, so a token can be redeemed twice under concurrent requests",
      "requirement": "A one-time-use credential (the reset token) must be consumed atomically: 'redeem exactly once' is a basic requirement for any single-use token, analogous to the double-spend problem in payment tokens.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:113-130: `reset_password` does `entry = self._resets.get(token)`, validates expiry/user, then later `del self._resets[token]`. Two concurrent calls with the same token can both pass the `entry is None` and expiry checks before either deletes the entry.",
      "failure": "If the service is ever run under a threaded/async server (the standard deployment for a Python web app), two simultaneous submissions of the same reset link -- e.g. a user double-clicking, or an attacker racing a legitimate request -- can both succeed, each writing `password_hash`, with no guarantee about which value ends up live and no indication to the user that a race occurred.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "unbounded-token-store-growth",
      "title": "Expired, unused reset tokens are never purged except on next request for the same user or on lookup of that exact token",
      "requirement": "State with a defined TTL (`TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`) must be reclaimed once it expires; an in-memory store that only prunes an entry when it happens to be looked up again is not bounded by its own stated expiry policy.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py:92-104: `_resets` is only cleaned for a given email when that same email calls `request_reset` again, or for a given token when `reset_password` happens to be called with it. There is no sweep of entries whose `expires_at` has passed without ever being touched again.",
      "failure": "In production, most requested resets are never completed (users ignore the email, or use a support-driven reset instead) and never revisited, so `_resets` grows without bound over the life of the process -- a slow memory leak that eventually degrades or crashes the account service.",
      "severity": "low"
    }
  ]
}
```
